_comment: Written email content for the 2026 Sundays. July-September was recovered from the original standalone liturgical_email_generator.html. October-December was drafted afterwards and its reading citations have NOT been checked against bible.usccb.org (that site returns an empty body to automated fetches, which is also why liturgical.js computes titles rather than scraping them) - verify each one against the USCCB link before sending, particularly Dec 27, where Holy Family has more than one permitted set of readings. Note Advent begins Nov 29 2026, starting a new liturgical year: gospels switch from Matthew (Year A) to Mark (Year B). Keyed by ISO date; each entry matches the `email` object the generator saves onto a week in months/{YYYY-MM}.weeks. Imported via the 'Import saved drafts' button, which skips any week already written.

2026-07-05.introMessage: This week’s gospel invites us into a spirit of rest and childlike trust in the Father — to lay down our burdens and learn from the one who is meek and humble of heart.

2026-07-12.gospel: Matthew 13:1–23 · The Parable of the Sower
2026-07-12.introMessage: This week’s gospel reminds us that the Word of God, when received in a ready and open heart, bears fruit beyond what we can imagine.

2026-07-19.gospel: Matthew 13:24–43 · The Parable of the Weeds
2026-07-19.introMessage: This week’s gospel calls us to patience and trust — God, in his wisdom, permits the wheat and weeds to grow together until the final harvest.

2026-07-26.gospel: Matthew 13:44–52 · The Treasure and the Pearl
2026-07-26.introMessage: This week’s gospel shows us that the Kingdom of Heaven is worth everything — like a treasure hidden in a field or a pearl of great price.

2026-08-02.gospel: Matthew 14:13–21 · The Feeding of the Five Thousand
2026-08-02.introMessage: This week’s gospel reveals Jesus as the one who multiplies our smallest offerings into abundance and feeds the hungry crowds with compassion.

2026-08-09.introMessage: This week’s gospel invites us to keep our eyes fixed on Jesus even when the winds and waves of life feel overwhelming — “Take courage, it is I; do not be afraid.”

2026-08-16.gospel: Matthew 15:21–28 · The Faith of the Canaanite Woman
2026-08-16.introMessage: This week’s gospel celebrates a faith that perseveres against every obstacle — a reminder that no one is outside the reach of God’s mercy.

2026-08-23.introMessage: This week’s gospel poses the question Jesus asked Peter — and asks each of us: “But who do you say that I am?”

2026-08-30.gospel: Matthew 16:21–27 · The First Prediction of the Passion
2026-08-30.introMessage: This week’s gospel calls us to take up our cross and follow Christ — not clinging to our own plans, but trusting in the Father’s will.

2026-09-06.introMessage: This week’s gospel gives us a beautiful framework for charity in community — to speak the truth with love and to seek one another’s genuine good.

2026-09-13.introMessage: This week’s gospel calls us to a radical forgiveness — not seven times, but seventy-seven times — because we ourselves have been forgiven so much.

2026-09-20.introMessage: This week’s gospel reminds us that God’s generosity cannot be measured by our expectations — his ways are higher than ours, and his mercy defies our calculations.

2026-09-27.gospel: Matthew 21:28–32 · The Parable of the Two Sons
2026-09-27.introMessage: This week’s gospel invites us to align our actions with our faith — to be people who don’t just say yes to God, but follow through.

2026-10-04.gospel: Matthew 21:33–43 · The Parable of the Tenants
2026-10-04.introMessage: This week’s gospel warns us not to withhold the fruits of the vineyard entrusted to us — God asks a return on the gifts he has given.

2026-10-11.gospel: Matthew 22:1–14 · The Parable of the Wedding Feast
2026-10-11.introMessage: This week’s gospel pictures the Kingdom as a wedding banquet — an invitation freely given, and a call to come clothed in readiness.

2026-10-18.introMessage: This week’s gospel draws the line between what belongs to Caesar and what belongs to God — and reminds us that we ourselves bear God’s image.

2026-10-25.introMessage: This week’s gospel gathers the whole law into two commands — to love God with everything we are, and our neighbor as ourselves.

2026-11-01.introMessage: This week we celebrate the whole company of saints — and hear the Beatitudes describe the shape of the life that leads there.

2026-11-08.introMessage: This week’s gospel asks whether our lamps are trimmed and ready — wisdom keeps oil in reserve for a bridegroom who comes at an unexpected hour.

2026-11-15.gospel: Matthew 25:14–30 · The Parable of the Talents
2026-11-15.introMessage: This week’s gospel calls us to risk what we have been given rather than bury it — the master rewards those who put his gifts to work.

2026-11-22.sundayName: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
2026-11-22.gospel: Matthew 25:31–46 · The Judgment of the Nations
2026-11-22.introMessage: This week we close the liturgical year with Christ the King — who tells us plainly that whatever we did for the least of these, we did for him.

2026-11-29.introMessage: This week we begin Advent, and a new liturgical year, with a single instruction repeated three times — watch, for you do not know when the Lord of the house is coming.

2026-12-06.gospel: Mark 1:1–8 · The Preaching of John the Baptist
2026-12-06.introMessage: This week John the Baptist calls out in the desert to prepare the way of the Lord — Advent’s invitation to make the paths straight in our own hearts.

2026-12-13.introMessage: This week, Gaudete Sunday, the Church tells us to rejoice — the light we have been waiting for is already standing among us, though we may not recognize him.

2026-12-20.introMessage: This week we hear Mary’s yes — the fiat that let God take flesh, and the model for our own trust in what we cannot yet see.

2026-12-27.sundayName: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph
2026-12-27.gospel: Luke 2:22–40 · The Presentation in the Temple
2026-12-27.introMessage: This week we honor the Holy Family, and watch Simeon and Anna recognize in a poor young family the salvation they had waited a lifetime to see.
